items.title: Malaysia, Pakistan to boost cooperation in fight against narcotics
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A proposed Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on narcotics cooperation will provide a more structured framework to strengthen existing collaboration between Malaysia and Pakistan in addressing current drug threats, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said discussions on the MoU were held during his visit to the Anti-Narcotics Force (ANF) Pakistan headquarters in Islamabad yesterday, where he received a briefing from its director-general, Major General Abdul Moeed. "Pakistan's position, which directly faces drug flows from Afghanistan, makes cooperation with the country important for Malaysia, especially as trafficking routes extend to East Asia and Southeast Asia.

items.title: Penang launches ONEMAP+ to track CCTVs, AEDs, and EV chargers across the state
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 22 — The Penang state government has launched ONEMAP+, a new digital platform designed to map the locations of closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras, automated external defibrillators (AEDs), and electric vehicle (EV) charging stations across the state. One platform, many benefits,” Chow said. Developed by PLANMalaysia Penang and the state Information and Communications Technology Division, the initiative incorporates data from the Penang Green Council, the Penang Island City Council (MBPP), the Seberang Perai City Council (MBSP), and the Penang Health Department.

items.title: US, Canada fail to reach trade pact to avert Trump tariffs
items.summary: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told reporters on Friday that "tonight, Canada declined to finalise the trade deal under the terms agreed earlier this week". The surprise announcement came after Trump said that the United States "should be able to have a deal with Canada", citing his "good relationship" with Carney. He said Canada was also maintaining its "prolonged retaliation" against the United States.

items.title: Safe internet campaign highlights parental role, social media ban for under-16s - Teo
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Efforts to raise parents' awareness of the ban on social media accounts for children under 16 will be intensified through the Safe Internet Campaign, said Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching. She said that although parents were still allowed to register digital accounts for their children, preventive measures and self-regulation at home were critical to complying with the government's current policy. These included 5,946 Sekolah Kebangsaan, 2,416 Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan, 1,285 Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Cina and 524 Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Tamil.

items.title: Immigration truck crash survivor keeps asking for husband who died
items.summary: A woman known as Arda shared that Norhayati Razali, 55, was still asking why her husband, Shaik Mohd Firdaus Shaikh Yahya, had yet to visit her in hospital. Arda's daughter, Udik, is friends with Norhayati and Shaik's daughter, Siti Darwisyah, 12, who was also killed in the crash, along with her older sister, Siti Nor Sazlin, 25. Arda shared a video of Udik recounting her visit to Norhayati, who suffered head, hand and leg injuries, at Kuala Lumpur Hospital.

items.title: Sara initiative boosts sales for Sabah retailers, wholesalers and manufacturers
items.summary: SEMPORNA: The Rahmah Basic Contribution (Sara) initiative is generating wider economic benefits in Sabah, with retailers, wholesalers and local manufacturers recording higher sales as more businesses join the programme and locally made products are added to its redemption list. Koperasi Anugerah Haji Badli chairman Sobri Lawdji said joining the Sara Merchant Partner programme late last year had significantly benefited the cooperative, which was established in early 2024 and is the only Sara Merchant Partner on Pulau Bum-Bum, Semporna. Sobri said the initiative had benefited more than 25,000 residents on the island who are eligible for Sara For All, including 3,300 recipients eligible for Sara Monthly and Rahmah Cash Aid (STR).

items.title: Malaysia calls for collective Asean action to tackle transboundary haze
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia is calling for collective action by all Asean member states to strengthen preparedness in addressing the risk of transboundary haze. This includes preventive measures, national preparedness and continuous monitoring, in line with the principles of the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution (AATHP). Arthur said that although fire incidents remained under control within the respective borders of member states, the risk of transboundary haze called for collective preparedness and heightened vigilance at the regional level.

items.title: Malaysia, 11 countries condemn Israeli strikes on Syria
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and 11 other countries have strongly condemned Israeli airstrikes targeting the Abu al-Duhur military airbase in northwestern Syria, describing the attacks as "an extreme escalation" and "a flagrant violation" of Syria's sovereignty, territorial integrity and political unity. "These attacks constitute an extreme escalation and a flagrant violation of the sovereignty, territorial integrity and political unity of the Syrian Arab Republic," the statement said. They stressed that Israel's continued violations of Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity risk further escalating tensions, undermining regional peace and stability, and eroding respect for international law and the principles of the United Nations (UN) Charter.

items.title: LPG cylinders explode after lorry catches fire on SILK Highway
items.summary: KAJANG: A lorry driver escaped unhurt while his attendant suffered burns after a lorry carrying gas cylinders caught fire before several cylinders exploded at Km0.1 of the SILK Highway yesterday. "Upon reaching Km0.1 of the SILK Highway, the 55-year-old lorry driver noticed that the gas cylinders being transported had caught fire. Naazron said the lorry was completely destroyed by fire.

items.title: Penang Port Commission says ferry ridership up 7pc in first half of 2026, announces free Merdeka rides
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 22 — Penang’s ferry services recorded a 7.28 per cent increase in passenger traffic between January and June this year compared to the same period in 2025. Penang Port Commission chairman Datuk Yeoh Soon Hin said that passenger volume in June alone reached 262,424. “These figures clearly reflect the sustained demand for ferry services as a key mode of public transportation in the state,” Yeoh said in a statement today.

items.title: Malaysia presses Asean for collective action on transboundary haze as El Niño peaks
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 22 — Malaysia is calling for collective action from all Asean member states to enhance preparedness in addressing the risk of transboundary haze through preventive measures, national preparedness and continuous monitoring, based on the principles of the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution (AATHP). Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said all member states needed to strengthen control measures and preparedness by maintaining close monitoring of high-risk areas, enhancing hotspot surveillance, strengthening enforcement of the ban on open burning, and ensuring efficient firefighting operational readiness. Arthur said that although fire incidents were still under control within the respective borders of member states, the risk of transboundary haze called for collective preparedness and heightened vigilance at the regional level.

items.title: Anwar, Sheikh Al-Azhar discuss efforts to deepen understanding of Islam
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Sheikh al-Azhar al-Sharif Prof Dr Ahmad al-Tayyeb discussed continuing dakwah efforts and Islamic studies to deepen religious understanding for the benefit of the wider community. "We also talked about continuing dakwah and study efforts to deepen the understanding of Islam. Anwar said he also brought up Sheikh al-Azhar al-Sharif's previous visit to Malaysia, which had left a deep impression on Muslims in the country.

items.title: Patriotic creations turn sewing hobby into income for Kuala Krai woman
items.summary: Her creativity in producing patriotic-themed and traditional clothing representing various races has received an encouraging response, particularly from parents who want their children to wear unique outfits for competitions and programmes held in conjunction with National Day celebrations. Aimi Aidora said that while she previously produced only a few sets of patriotic-themed clothing, this year she had successfully completed 12 sets of traditional women's clothing and three sets of men's clothing representing various races, including Malays, Chinese and Indians. However, when I received positive feedback from customers, I started adding traditional clothing from various races to my collection to give students more choices.

items.title: Serian API drops to 190 as Sarawak air quality improves slightly
items.summary: Meanwhile, 57 areas nationwide recorded API readings at the moderate level. An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and readings above 300 hazardous. API data is released hourly based on readings recorded at 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide.

items.title: Perak youth urged to bridge skills gap as investments surge
items.summary: "Approved investments also reached RM15.76 billion and are expected to create 10,704 job opportunities," he said. Saarani said this in his speech at the opening of the fifth session of the Perak Youth Assembly at Bangunan Perak Darul Ridzuan here today. he said.

items.title: No more walk-ins: Malaysia’s foreign worker recruitment now entirely online
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 22 — Applications for the recruitment of foreign workers are now fully processed online through the Foreign Workers Centralised Management System (FWCMS), eliminating the need for employers to submit applications manually or make walk-in visits from today The Ministry of Human Resources (Kesuma) said the digitalisation initiative aims to simplify the process by reducing repeated visits to government offices, shortening waiting times and making the overall procedure more organised and transparent. “All applications remain subject to scrutiny, relevant laws, eligibility requirements, foreign worker employment policies and reviews by the relevant Regulatory Agencies (AKS),” it said in a statement. Kesuma said the application process begins with employers obtaining prior approval to hire foreign workers under Section 60K of the Employment Act 1955, until the issuance of a Conditional Approval Letter (SKB).

items.title: Terengganu village on alert after wild elephant destroys banana, sugarcane crops
items.summary: KUALA NERUS, Aug 22 — The Terengganu Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) is investigating a complaint about a wild elephant reportedly roaming in Kampung Pengkalan Gelugor, Jeram, here yesterday. State Perhilitan director Dennis Ten Choon Yung said investigations found that the elephant had destroyed residents’ crops, including banana and sugarcane plants, while also roaming around the village and posing a safety risk to residents. “Residents are also urged to give the department space to carry out control and translocation operations when conditions permit,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: 'Mak Siti' gold mining syndicate making RM13,000 a day busted
items.summary: MARANG: An illegal gold mining syndicate earning up to RM13,000 a day was busted after police detained 15 people in a raid at Bukit Kor. The General Operations Force (GOF) also seized mining equipment and heavy machinery worth an estimated RM449,000 during the operation. Radzi said the syndicate excavated pits about 6m deep before crushing, washing, filtering and screening the material to extract gold.

items.title: Teacher, 6-year-old son killed after MPV skids into ditch
items.summary: KUANTAN: A teacher and her 6-year-old son were killed after the multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) they were travelling in skidded at Km149 of Jalan Kuantan-Seremban near Kampung Bukit Serok, Muadzam Shah, here yesterday. District police chief Superintendent Sharif Shai Sharif Mondoi said the family of three was travelling from Seremban, Negri Sembilan, to Felda Keratong 1 in Muadzam Shah when the incident occurred. The MPV driver, Mohd Azmi Mohahir, 47, was seriously injured and is receiving treatment at Muadzam Shah Hospital here.

items.title: Foreign worker applications now fully online from today
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Employers seeking to recruit foreign workers will no longer need to submit applications manually or make walk-in visits to government offices, with the entire process now conducted online through the Foreign Workers Centralised Management System (FWCMS). However, the ministry said the move did not mean that requirements for hiring foreign workers had been relaxed. The ministry said the application process begins with employers obtaining prior approval to hire foreign workers under Section 60K of the Employment Act 1955, and ends with the issuance of a Conditional Approval Letter (SKB).

items.title: Teacher and son die after MPV hits debris and plunges into ravine in Rompin
items.summary: Rompin police chief Supt Sharif Shai Sharif Mondoi said the accident, which occurred at about 9.30 pm, claimed the lives of Kartinie Ngatenan, 46, and her six-year-old son Muhammad Akif Mohd Azmi at the scene. He said preliminary investigations found that the accident occurred when the multipurpose vehicle (MPV), driven by the victim’s 47-year-old husband, was travelling from Seremban, Negeri Sembilan, towards Felda Keratong in Rompin. Sharif Shai said the case was being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.

items.title: Pick-up truck crashes into house after hitting motorcycle
items.summary: GUA MUSANG: A pick-up truck skidded and hit a motorcycle before crashing into a house along Jalan Kampung Kerinting here yesterday. In the 4.55pm incident, the 53-year-old motorcyclist suffered injuries to his left leg and was treated at Gua Musang Hospital. "The motorcyclist suffered minor injuries to his left leg and is still receiving treatment at Gua Musang Hospital," he said.

items.title: MCBA foils attempt to smuggle 45 animal horns through Penang airport
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) has foiled an attempt to smuggle 45 pieces of suspected animal horns worth RM5,000 through Penang International Airport. The passenger was found carrying the suspected wildlife products without a permit or valid documentation, an offence under Section 68(1)(b) of the Wildlife Conservation Act. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Prince Harry and others ordered to pay millions over failed lawsuit
items.summary: LONDON: Britain's Prince Harry, singer Elton John and other high-profile claimants face paying millions of dollars out of their own pockets to cover the legal costs of the Daily Mail's publisher after a judge ruled their failed privacy lawsuits were conducted in an unreasonable way. Judge Matthew Nicklin's judgment on costs, published on Friday, ordered an interim payment from the claimants of £9.54 million, due by August 28, towards the legal costs of Associated Newspapers. In a further damaging blow, Nicklin said the additional costs should be paid on an "indemnity basis", meaning Associated does not need to show they were reasonable and proportionate.

items.title: Terengganu Perhilitan probes wild elephant sighting, residents advised to stay away
items.summary: KUALA NERUS: The Terengganu Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) is investigating a complaint about a wild elephant reportedly roaming in Kampung Pengkalan Gelugor, Jeram, here yesterday. State Perhilitan director Dennis Ten Choon Yung said investigations found that the elephant had destroyed residents' crops, including banana and sugarcane plants, while roaming around the village and posing a safety risk to residents. "Residents are also urged to give the department space to carry out control and translocation operations when conditions permit," he said in a statement today.

items.title: Police record Hadi's statement over his article, says aide
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have recorded a statement from Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang over one of his articles, his aide said. His political secretary, Mohd Syahir Sulaiman, told the New Straits Times that the Marang member of Parliament had his statement recorded in Kuala Lumpur last week. Syahir, who is also Pas assistant secretary-general, said police launched an investigation into Hadi following reports lodged by DAP supporters.

items.title: Comfort zone keeping Bumiputera firms off Bursa, says PNB chief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A lack of strategic planning to scale Bumiputera companies remains the primary barrier preventing them from being listed on Bursa Malaysia, says the head of one of the country's largest fund management companies. Permodalan Nasional Bhd president and group chief executive Datuk Rizal Rickman Ramli said many Bumiputera firms were reluctant to undertake bold transformation as they were comfortable operating as they were. Rizal said some entrepreneurs put growth aspirations on the back burner once their businesses performed well and reached a comfort zone.

items.title: Chew Swee Yoke, Malaysia’s legal aid pioneer and lawyer in Anwar’s ‘black eye’ case, dies at 81
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 22 — Chew Swee Yoke, a pioneering Malaysian lawyer, advocate for justice and proud Victorian, passed away on the morning of August 18, aged 81. In 1982, Chew established the first Legal Aid Centre in Kuala Lumpur and became the first Chairperson of the Bar Council Legal Aid Committee. The Malaysian Bar recognises her as a pioneer of legal aid in Malaysia.

items.title: Haze: 10 Sarawak areas record unhealthy API readings, Serian highest at 191
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Ten areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 7.30am today, with Serian recording the highest reading at 191. Based on the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, other areas registering unhealthy API readings included Kuching (181), Samarahan (178), Sri Aman (174) and Sarikei (171). Bukit Rambai in Melaka was the only area outside Sarawak to record an unhealthy API reading, at 140.

items.title: Exco: Perak and federal governments streamlining laws for Pulau Sembilan enforcement
items.summary: SUNGAI SIPUT, Aug 22 — The Perak and federal governments are upgrading existing legislation to streamline and strengthen enforcement operations in the waters of the Pulau Sembilan State Park. Perak Tourism, Industry, Investment and Corridor Development Committee chairman Loh Sze Yee said the move aimed to address overlapping jurisdictions between the two parties, which had made comprehensive enforcement difficult. The Pulau Sembilan State Park was officially closed to the public on April 1, 2017, following severe damage to its marine ecosystem and coral reef structures caused by encroachment and uncontrolled tourism activities.

items.title: Penang police warn convoy participants: No sirens, no stunts, no controlling traffic
items.summary: “The assessment will take into account the route, number of participants, timing, stopover locations and current traffic conditions to ensure the convoy can proceed in an orderly manner without affecting safety, public order and traffic flow,” he said in a statement yesterday. He said organisers and participants must also comply with all laws and road regulations, as well as follow the instructions of police and traffic officers. Lim said organisers must also take into account ongoing construction work, lane closures and traffic diversions when planning the convoy route and timing.

items.title: #NSTviral: Netizens urge DBKL action over stall blocking Sentul walkway
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Netizens have urged Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) to take swift enforcement action against an unauthorised street stall in Kampung Batu, Sentul, after it obstructed a public five-foot walkway. Threads user @bungaeomma posted photos highlighting the safety hazards and inconvenience caused to pedestrians by the stall. "Trade properly and legally without disturbing others," the user wrote.

items.title: Thai police detain two Kelantan men for possession of 1,560 Epam pills
items.summary: NARATHIWAT, Aug 22 — Two Malaysians were detained by Thai police in Sungai Kolok here on Thursday night after authorities found 1,560 Epam (Nitrazepam) tablets believed to be in their possession. Sungai Kolok Police Chief Col Thun Sirikhunt, when contacted by Bernama, said the two suspects, aged 24 and 30 and from Kelantan, were detained at about 10.30 pm in front of a restaurant on Jalan Anukachart Usorn in Sungai Kolok town, following intelligence gathering and information from members of the public. Thun said the drugs, classified as a Category 2 psychotropic substance, were packed in 39 blister packs, each containing 40 tablets, with a total estimated value of 10,608 baht (about RM1,310).

items.title: Penang Hospital acts to cut emergency wait times after viral video shows overcrowding
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 22 — The Penang Health Department (JKNPP) is implementing several measures to reduce congestion and waiting times at the Emergency and Trauma Department of Penang Hospital (HPP), particularly during peak hours. Penang Health director Dr Zulhizzam Abdullah said a short-term measure involves upgrading space at the HPP Outpatient Department block to expand treatment areas and integrate patient flow from the Emergency and Trauma Department. “JKNPP takes note of the video that went viral on social media last night regarding the long waiting time at the HPP Emergency and Trauma Department.

items.title: Malaysia, Pakistan strengthen legal ties with new prisoner transfer treaty
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 22 — Malaysia and Pakistan yesterday signed the International Transfer of Prisoners (ITOP) Treaty, strengthening legal and security cooperation between the two countries. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the treaty was signed with Pakistan’s Interior and Narcotics Control Minister Syed Mohsin Raza Naqvi following his courtesy call on Pakistan Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif. “This signing marks another important milestone in Malaysia-Pakistan bilateral relations, particularly in strengthening security and legal cooperation between the two countries,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday.

items.title: Anwar and Pakistans’s Shehbaz call for diplomacy in Iran-US tensions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 22 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his Pakistani counterpart Shehbaz Sharif have agreed that regional tensions must be addressed through dialogue and diplomacy to safeguard peace and stability. Anwar said the shared position was reached during a telephone conversation with Shehbaz, during which they exchanged views on current regional developments and the latest developments in Iran-US relations. In a Facebook post, Anwar said Shehbaz also enquired about his health during the telephone conversation.

items.title: Technology, construction to gain as expanded FBM KLCI cuts bank, utility weights [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The expansion of the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) is set to dilute the dominance of banking and utilities, with technology, construction and consumer sectors emerging as the key beneficiaries, analysts said. Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) said technology is expected to be the biggest winner among the new sectors entering the FBM KLCI following its expansion from December 2026. The sector is projected to account for 1.9 per cent of the index weighting in phase one and 3.4 per cent in phase two, from no representation currently.

items.title: Iran threatens military response to US sanctions
items.summary: DUBAI: Iran said on Friday that its response to any new US threats would be "devastating" after Washington pledged to impose the toughest financial penalties in history with the aim of toppling the Iranian leadership. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he would give details on Monday of the planned sanctions, after President Donald Trump warned of economic consequences against any country that provided "any type of lifeline to Iran". The chief of staff of Iran's Armed Forces, Major General Ali Abdollahi, said the Islamic Republic's reaction would be broad and decisive.

items.title: US Supreme Court allows White House ballroom construction for now
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The US Supreme Court on Friday allowed construction of a massive White House ballroom to continue for now, giving President Donald Trump a temporary victory for one of his pet renovation projects. Chief Justice John Roberts temporarily lifted a lower court ruling that had demanded a halt to construction of the controversial ballroom by midnight on Friday. The Trump administration asked the conservative-dominated Supreme Court last week to allow it to finish building the ballroom and an underground bunker at the White House, saying the project was essential for national security.

items.title: Pahang coastline needs early action as erosion risks grow
items.summary: KUANTAN: Pahang's direct exposure to South China Sea makes its coastline increasingly vulnerable to stronger waves and extreme weather, highlighting the need for early action to tackle coastal erosion. The effects of coastal erosion are gradual but becoming increasingly visible, particularly along the southern part of Pahang. "Pekan, including Nenasi and Rompin, are among the areas showing signs of coastal erosion."

items.title: Pahang seeks RM850m to tackle erosion along 61km coastline
items.summary: KUANTAN: The Pahang government has implemented short- and long-term measures to address coastal erosion along 61km of coastline in the Pekan, Rompin and Kuantan districts. State Public Works, Transport and Health Committee chairman Datuk Razali Kassim said the Irrigation and Drainage Department conducted studies and kept records to identify the causes of coastal erosion and determine appropriate measures. He said coastal erosion was a year-round issue requiring continuous monitoring and action, particularly where it could affect homes, public infrastructure and access routes.

items.title: Waves sweep away home, memories in Rompin village [WATCH]
items.summary: The three-room house was sponsored by a financial institution for her family in 2009. They did not expect giant waves during the monsoon season on Jan 12 last year to bring down one of its walls, forcing them to leave the village. During the incident last year, the sea was barely 20m away.

items.title: RM700,000 seaside dream swept away by coastal erosion [WATCH]
items.summary: Tourism entrepreneur Edde Firdaus Abdul Aziz had invested some RM700,000 to acquire 1ha of coastal land, transforming it into Kekunang Tering Chalet, a nature getaway featuring seven chalets, including a tree house and tube cabins fashioned from concrete culverts. But the dream lasted only about six years before relentless coastal erosion claimed the structures one by one. Edde Firdaus, 46, said the sea had since devoured much of the land, leaving just 0.4ha, with the remaining ground continuing to disappear.

items.title: Trump announces temporary tariff relief on ground beef imports
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump announced on Friday that the United States would temporarily allow a greater volume of foreign beef imports, in his latest bid to lower costs for American consumers as midterm elections approach. The US cattle herd has shrunk to its lowest level since the 1950s – in part due to drought and international competition – with the diminishing numbers pushing beef product prices higher. 'DISAPPOINTED' US cattle and rancher groups have been resistant to importing more beef.

items.title: From a Penang home kitchen to nationwide favourite: The story of Jeruk Madu Pak Ali
items.summary: More than four decades later, Jeruk Madu Pak Ali has grown from a three-person operation to a business with four production plants in Simpang Ampat on mainland Penang with over 100 employees and 50 retail outlets nationwide. Together, the facilities produce about 300 tonnes of pickled fruits every month. Jeruk Madu Pak Ali’s marketing and public relations executive Mohd Shahrul Nizam Shahidin showing the packaged pickled fruits and the traditional trades certificate from Penang Global Tourism.

items.title: Tebrau MP to raise in Parliament tax uncertainty over commingled oil cargo
items.summary: He said the matter required clarification from the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (RMCD) to ensure industry players had clarity and certainty regarding their tax obligations. As such, I hope and urge the Royal Customs to provide greater clarity on this matter to industry players. Puah said he would raise the matter in Parliament to seek clarification on the tax treatment of commingled oil cargo operations.

items.title: Independent review, not blind denial, needed to address US transshipment claims, says maritime trade expert
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — Malaysia should conduct an independent review into allegations by the United States (US) concerning transshipment activities to ensure any violations are identified while protecting the country’s reputation, according to Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan. The maritime expert said the review must trace the complete movement of the cargo, including the manifest, bill of lading, Customs documentation, certificate of origin, storage records, any blending or processing carried out and the final declaration before export. “Malaysia must respond quickly with evidence, independent verification and a clear enforcement position.

items.title: Zahid: Melaka election strategy cannot mirror Johor, Negeri Sembilan, needs tailored formula
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — Barisan Nasional (BN) needs a formula suitable to Melaka’s geopolitical landscape in the upcoming state election, said its chairman, Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. He said any negotiations must take into account two aspects, namely benefits and drawbacks. He said political cooperation at the state level should also be seen in the context of efforts to strengthen political stability at the national level.

items.title: Anwar lands in Brunei for 27th Annual Leaders’ Consultation, to meet Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah
items.summary: BANDAR SERI BEGAWAN, Aug 21 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim arrived here today for a two-day working visit to attend the 27th Annual Leaders’ Consultation (ALC-27) between Malaysia and Brunei. The special aircraft carrying Anwar and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, landed at Brunei International Airport at 6.10pm. In 2025, total trade between Malaysia and Brunei was recorded at RM5.86 billion (US$1.37 billion), with exports to Brunei valued at RM4.20 billion (US$0.98 billion) and imports at RM1.66 billion (US$0.39 billion).

items.title: Sarawak haze fight hinges on suitable clouds, Uggah says seeding useless without them
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 21 — Cloud seeding operations to tackle the haze will depend on favourable weather conditions, particularly the presence of suitable clouds, said Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas. The State Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) chairman said discussions had been held with the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), which was ready to conduct the cloud seeding operation whenever weather conditions permit. Uggah expressed hope that weather conditions would improve soon, allowing the cloud seeding operation to be carried out and help tackle the haze.

items.title: Perhilitan captures giant 5.5‑metre crocodile after May attack injured retired policeman in Negeri Sembilan
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 21 — The Negeri Sembilan Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) captured a 500kg crocodile measuring 5.5 metres in Sungai Tanjung Agas, Sungai Linggi, today. Its director, Wan Mat Wan Harun, said the female crocodile, estimated at 70 years old, was captured in a trap placed in the area two days ago. “Perhilitan set a crocodile trap at the site on Wednesday following a report about the reptile in Tanjung Agas.

items.title: Court of Appeal spares two men gallows, orders 30 years jail plus 12 rotan strokes
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 21 — Two men escaped the gallows after the Court of Appeal substituted their death sentences with 30 years’ imprisonment and 12 strokes of the cane each for drug trafficking. The decision was made by a three-member panel comprising Datuk Azmi Ariffin (now a Federal Court judge), Datuk Hayatul Akmal Abdul Aziz and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid, who dismissed Muhamad Nor Aziz and Muhamad Shafiq Aliff Mazlan’s appeals against their convictions. Judge Meor Hashimi said the two appellants had instead received a fair and impartial trial and were given adequate opportunity to defend themselves by the trial judge.

items.title: Zahid urges Malaysian bikers abroad to obey host laws after Hat Yai summons row
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — Malaysian motorsport enthusiasts travelling abroad must abide by the laws and regulations of their host countries, says Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. He said mutual respect, tolerance and an understanding of neighbouring countries’ regulations were crucial to maintaining good relations among Asean member states. Ahmad Zahid said this when met by reporters after the closing ceremony of the Negeri Sembilan Contingent Charity Ride programme with the Ipoh Super Bike Club (ISBC) in conjunction with the 219th Police Day and 69th Merdeka Eve celebrations at the Kuala Lumpur Police Contingent Headquarters here today.

items.title: Chow says Penang awaits DAP leadership call before equal constituency law move
items.summary: BATU KAWAN, Aug 21 — Penang will await a decision from DAP’s national leadership before considering any move to introduce an Equal Constituency Development Enactment in the state, said Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow. He said opposition representatives regularly raise the matter during State Legislative Assembly sittings and seek higher allocations. Chow said opposition assemblymen currently receive RM60,000 in allocation.

items.title: Police vow transparent Tabung Haji investigations, warn public against speculation or rumours
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), through its Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID), has opened five investigation papers into cases involving Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), including matters raised in the Tabung Haji Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report. CCID director Datuk Rusdi Mohd Isa said 127 people had so far had their statements recorded to assist the investigations. He said the investigations were being conducted under several laws, including the Penal Code, Tabung Haji Act 1995, Companies Act 1965 and Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (AMLATFPUAA).

items.title: Foreign minister says Asean best platform as Malaysia pushes regional action on haze crisis
items.summary: BANDAR SERI BEGAWAN, Aug 21 — Malaysia will utilise Asean diplomatic channels to seek a solution to the transboundary haze affecting several areas in the region, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan. He said Asean remains the most appropriate platform for addressing issues involving countries in the region. “NRES Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup will also write to his counterpart in Indonesia.

items.title: Rapid KL to run 24‑hour trains and buses for Merdeka Eve and National Day crowds
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — Selected rail and bus services operated by Rapid KL will operate 24 hours on Aug 30 and 31 to facilitate public movement in conjunction with the 2026 National Day celebrations. Rapid KL in a statement today announced that the extension of operating hours involves all its rail services, namely the Light Rail Transit (LRT), Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) and Kuala Lumpur Monorail. “The Sunway BRT (Bus Rapid Transit) Line, along with several bus routes and Rapid KL On-Demand (ROD), will also operate 24 hours, providing more travel options to the public throughout the celebration period.

items.title: Ten GOF personnel detained in Penang extortion probe involving e-waste factory
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — Ten General Operations Force (GOF) personnel from the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) were detained yesterday to assist investigations into an extortion case at an electronic waste processing factory in Tasik Gelugor, Penang. Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (Operations) deputy director Datuk Muhammad Abdul Halim said all the personnel involved were stationed at the GOF 2nd Battalion in Kulim, Kedah. Any officer or personnel involved in any crime, the force’s management will take appropriate action without favouritism,” he told a press conference here today.

items.title: Company MD says he handed Hamzah Zainudin’s former aide RM350,000 cash in paper bags after firm won police tender
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — A witness told the Sessions Court today that Sayed Amir Muzzakkir Al Sayed Mohamad asked him to pay RM350,000 in cash as part of a five per cent commission after helping Nexuscorpgroup Sdn Bhd (NXG) secure a Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) project tender. “Sayed (Sayed Amir Muzzakkir) contacted me and asked me, ‘Can you pay 350k?, I need to use this money, cash.’ “I also informed Sayed that I would pay in two instalments and Sayed agreed to that proposal,” said the main prosecution witness while reading his witness statement at the corruption trial of Sayed Amir Muzzakkir, who is facing three charges involving RM350,000.

items.title: PAS tells BN to choose between Perikatan and Pakatan in Melaka
items.summary: MARANG, Aug 21 — PAS President Abdul Hadi Awang said Perikatan Nasional is fully prepared to walk away from Barisan Nasional (BN) should its partner flirt with an alliance with Pakatan Harapan (PH) for the Melaka state election. Hadi said that while the PN coalition remains confident in its ability to deploy a range of tactical alternatives, high-level discussions regarding cooperation with BN for the Melaka polls remain ongoing, NST reported. Hadi further observed that the complexities faced during the Johor state election appear to have subsided, making the path toward a Melaka alliance more straightforward.
